logLevelRemap.matchMessage: /^pip-compile: dependency not found in lock file$/

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Open a security PR the moment an advisory lands instead of waiting for the weekly schedule. osvVulnerabilityAlerts covers the uv/pip-compile *.lock files that GitHub's native Dependabot does not parse. Renovate applies this block as a `force` package rule appended AFTER the packageRules below (workers/repository/init/vulnerability.ts), carrying its own defaults for the alert: minimumReleaseAge null, schedule [], prCreation immediate, groupName null. So a security PR is ungrouped, opens at once and skips the three-day gate; whether it then merges itself is decided by the same packageRules as any other update. A security patch, or a security minor of dev tooling, of pyyaml, of a CI-path action or of a pinned release binary, automerges once ci-ok is green and carries no manual-merge label; a security major, or a security minor of sigstore or of a release-only action, opens for review. `addLabels` (not `labels`) so `security` stacks on whatever label the update rules left instead of replacing it. This is the continuous-detection half of the pip-audit split (PR audit informational, publish audit blocking — see .github/workflows/ci.yml). Verified against Renovate 44.157.

pip-compile.description: The 16 'dependency not found in lock file' warnings, all against requirements-build.lock, are EXPECTED. Do not restructure the locks — or revert the lock-header style — to silence them. They date from #333 (2026-06-09), which rewrote the uv headers to the parseable long form (--extra=X, --output-file=Y): before that Renovate threw a header-parse error and this manager tracked nothing at all, so the warnings are the visible cost of pip-compile coverage actually working. #472 (2026-08-07) took the count 15 -> 16 by adding mkdocs-material. They surface on the Dependency Dashboard as a single deduped 'Repository Problems' bullet (workers/repository/common.ts keys the set on level+message, so all 16 collapse into one), and only on runs where extraction is not served from the repo cache (cache key = base-branch SHA + config hash + manager fingerprints) — so the section appeared and disappeared between runs rather than being permanent. The logLevelRemap entry at the top of this file now demotes that exact message to debug so it never reaches the dashboard (verified 16 -> 0 warnings with dep extraction byte-identical). This suppresses nothing that worked: because the problem set dedupes on level+message, a genuine 17th occurrence was ALREADY invisible — it collapsed into the same single bullet as the 16 expected ones. The message still appears under LOG_LEVEL=debug. Note the remap matches on message text only (getRemappedLevel receives just the string), so it cannot be scoped to requirements-build.lock; a real missing-lock-dep elsewhere is also demoted, and in practice surfaces instead as a CI failure when something imports the absent dep. Cause: Renovate parses --extra out of each lock header into compileArgs.extra (manager/pip-compile/common.ts) but the dep-matching loop (manager/pip-compile/extract.ts) never consults it — it compares every pep621 dep in pyproject.toml against one lock and warns for each one absent, with no notion that --extra was meant to narrow the set. A guard in that same loop means only the FIRST lock referencing pyproject.toml runs the comparison, and that is alphabetically-first requirements-build.lock, whose --extra=container set is our narrowest (build, plus the PyYAML runtime dep) — so the noise is worst-case by accident of filename ordering. The 16 are: requires-python and hatchling (build-system.requires, which can never appear in a pip lock), the intentional compose-lint[lint] self-reference, and optional-dependency pins that legitimately live in requirements-dev.lock / requirements-docs.lock / requirements.lock (including the corpus/matplotlib group deliberately absent from every lock). Update coverage is NOT affected: verified 2026-08-08 with `npx renovate@latest --platform=local --dry-run=extract` that each warned dep is still extracted with its currentValue and datasource=pypi and no skipReason, so bumps still open normally; only lockedVersion, a display field, goes unset. No upstream issue tracked this as of 2026-08-08; the fix would be for that loop to skip deps whose managerData.depGroup falls outside compileArgs.extra (pep621 already tags them) and to skip the requires-python / build-system.requires depTypes.

poetry.description: pyproject.toml is already covered by pep621 + pip-compile. The poetry manager detects the same [project] deps but is not in the python group rule, so it spawned duplicate ungrouped PRs that bumped pyproject without regenerating the lockfiles (e.g. renovate/ruff-0.x, #329).

customManagers.description: The Docker Compose plugin the differential suites are graded against. The runner image pins its own — images/ubuntu/toolsets/toolset-2404.json in actions/runner-images holds it at 2.38.2 while docker/compose is on 5.x — and that version is not a choice this project made: CI was grading ADR-036's include: orderings, every one measured on Compose 5.5.0, against a binary that refuses the documents describing them ('services.web conflicts with imported resource'). .github/scripts/install-compose-plugin.sh installs the pin ahead of the image's copy; this manager moves it. Patch and minor bumps automerge under the custom.regex rule below: ci.yml is in the `code` change filter, so the bump PR runs the differential suites it exists to re-prove, and a green run means the new binary still agrees with every graded ordering. A red run is precisely the PR that has to be triaged into 'Compose changed', 'we were wrong', or 'a new deliberate divergence', and Renovate never merges a red PR, so that triage still reaches a human.

Release binaries that ci.yml jobs download from a GitHub Release and verify against the release's checksums file (actionlint, hadolint). The version is a bare X.Y.Z literal beside a `# renovate:` annotation; the tag carries a v prefix, so extractVersion strips it. Patch and minor bumps automerge under the custom.regex rule below: each bump runs the linter it bumps on the PR itself (ci.yml is in the `workflows` change filter for actionlint and in the `dockerfile` filter for hadolint), so a green run is the review and a red one waits for a human with the tool's release notes.

Container images the premise validator runs (busybox, and python:3.13-alpine for the checks busybox cannot express). They are string constants in a Python script, which no built-in manager reads, so until this manager existed both digests sat where they were pinned (busybox from May 2026, python from June) with nothing to say they were stale. Each pin is a `# renovate: datasource=docker depName=…` line, then `NAME = (`, then one string `"name:tag@sha256:<index digest>"`; the tag is what Renovate looks the digest up by. Digest refreshes automerge under the Docker Hub digest rule below, because the rule-premises job re-runs every premise against the new image on the PR; a tag change (busybox 1.39, python 3.14-alpine) is a minor and opens with manual-merge.

packageRules.description: GitHub Actions: SHA-pin every uses: with version comment (CLAUDE.md).

Workflows that run only after the tag is pushed (publish.yml and the reusable workflows it calls) get their own group. Minors split by whether the action also runs on the CI path: the nine that do are exercised on the PR itself and automerge under their own rule below, while a minor of the five that run only after the tag (actions/attest-build-provenance, anchore/sbom-action, pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish, sigstore/cosign-installer, sigstore/gh-action-sigstore-python) is exercised for the first time at release, after the irreversible trigger, so it keeps manual-merge and holds the group for a human. Separate groups because Renovate automerges a group only when every update in it is eligible: one release-path minor would otherwise hold the whole weekly batch for a human.

Python runtime + dev deps batched into one PR. pip-compile tracks the uv-generated requirements*.lock files: their .lock extension is matched by no pip-family manager by default, leaving transitive pins (e.g. urllib3) invisible to Renovate and weekly lockFileMaintenance a no-op for these files.
Docker base images: digest-pin per CLAUDE.md.

Production runtime + build-stage base images bypass the weekly schedule. Debian and distroless rebuilds carry CVE patches we cannot apply ourselves (no shell, no apt at runtime), so opening the bump PR same-day shrinks the window between upstream patch and our published image. Whether the bump then merges itself is decided by the Docker Hub digest rule at the end of this list: debian does, distroless cannot (gcr.io gives Renovate no release timestamp to age against).

Demo toolchain: the compose-lint pin in scripts/demo records which release the committed GIF was rendered on, so it moves only as part of a deliberate demo regeneration (docs/RELEASING.md), never via Renovate. pillow/numpy and transitives in the same lock stay managed.

Forgejo smoke harness: NOT Renovate's. The hosted runner cannot look up codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo or data.forgejo.org/forgejo/runner (Dependency Dashboard: 'no-result' + 'Error obtaining docker token', while a local `renovate --platform=local --dry-run=lookup` resolves both — the hosted runner's egress, not the registries), so the same-day bump rule that replaced #748's tests/ move never produced a PR, and a Renovate PR could not pass anyway: forgejo-smoke asserts docs/forgejo.md's 'Verified on Forgejo X, runner Y' line against the live stack, and Renovate cannot move that line. forgejo-smoke-bump.yml owns both files instead (daily; scripts/forgejo_smoke_bump.py). Disabled here so two writers never race on the same pin; the file stays listed on the dashboard for visibility.

Automerge low-risk routine updates once CI is green. Patch-level Python dep bumps, pinned-digest refreshes for GitHub Actions, and lockFileMaintenance go in without human review. Docker digests have their own rule at the end of this list (Docker Hub only; it explains why). minimumReleaseAge is the one human-shaped gate on that path: a release merges itself only after it has been public for three days, which is the window in which a compromised or broken upstream release is usually pulled or yanked. Hash-locked installs do not help here — they pin whatever release was current. The PR still opens at once; Renovate holds a renovate/stability-days check pending until the age passes, then automerge proceeds. platformAutomerge is deliberately FALSE so that gate cannot be routed around: GitHub's native auto-merge lands a PR as soon as its REQUIRED checks pass, and the only required check here is ci-ok — renovate/stability-days is not one, so a platform-armed PR could merge inside the three days the option exists to enforce. Renovate merging on its own, after its own checks, is the behaviour this repo has always had (platform auto-merge was unavailable at repo level until the marketplace-pin job needed it), so this pins it rather than changes it. Security PRs are unaffected: vulnerabilityAlerts defaults minimumReleaseAge to null, so an OSV fix still lands immediately. Its updates carry no label: `labels: []` replaces the repo-wide `manual-merge` default. Not an `automerge` label, because a grouped PR (python, github-actions) takes the union of its updates' labels, while Renovate automerges a group only when EVERY update in it is eligible (`config.automerge = upgrades.every(...)` in workers/repository/updates/generate.ts). A mixed group therefore carried both labels and still needed a human. With no label on the eligible side, a PR has `manual-merge` exactly when at least one update in it is not automerge-eligible, which is exactly when Renovate will not merge it. A template cannot pick the label per PR instead: `automerge` is not an allowed template field. Verified against Renovate 44.117.

Minor bumps of Python dev tooling automerge too. Every optional-dependency group (lint, security, docs, dev, corpus, container) is installed and exercised by a PR gate (ruff, mypy, pytest, bandit, pip-audit, mkdocs, the Docker build), so a green run is the review. The runtime dependency (project.dependencies: pyyaml) has its own rule below: its minors move the locks only, never the wheel's range. sigstore is excluded: it must move in lockstep with the sigstore/gh-action-sigstore-python action that signs what it verifies (the pin's comment in pyproject.toml), and that action's minors are manual, so a sigstore minor opens for review alongside it. twine is not excluded: ci.yml's dist-check job builds the sdist and wheel and runs `twine check --strict` on every PR that touches code or the locks, so a twine minor is exercised before the tag like any other dev tool. pep621 and pip-compile tag deps with the same depType (verified with `renovate --platform=local --dry-run=extract` on 44.132), so the pyproject edit and the lock regeneration are both eligible and the grouped PR automerges as a whole.

Minor bumps of actions on the CI path automerge. Every action here is SHA-pinned and runs in the PR's own workflow, so the bump tests itself. The release-path workflows are carved into the github-actions-release group above and excluded here; the rule after this one takes their minors for the actions that also run on the CI path, and the release-only actions' minors keep the manual-merge label. Majors, including the ubuntu runner image (datasource github-runners), stay manual.

Minor bumps of release-path actions that ALSO run on the CI path automerge. These nine are SHA-pinned in ci.yml and the other PR and push workflows as well, so the same minor runs on the PR before it ever runs after a tag, and the github-actions-release group then holds only eligible updates and merges itself. The five actions that run only after the tag are deliberately not listed (see the group's description above): their minors keep manual-merge and hold the group for a human, because a first run after the irreversible trigger is not a review. depName is the owner/repo part of `uses:`, so github/codeql-action covers its upload-sarif sub-action (verified with `renovate --platform=local --dry-run=extract` on 44.157).

Patch and minor bumps of the release binaries ci.yml downloads (the custom regex managers above: docker/compose, rhysd/actionlint, hadolint/hadolint) automerge. Each bump runs the tool it bumps on the PR, so a green run is the review. Compose: the plugin is what the differential suites grade against, and ci.yml is in the `code` change filter, so the bump re-runs every suite that could disagree with the new binary; green means no loader rule moved under us. actionlint: ci.yml is in the `workflows` filter, so the bumped linter runs over every workflow. hadolint: ci.yml is in the `dockerfile` filter for exactly this, so the bumped linter runs over the Dockerfile. Red stays manual on all three, because Renovate merges only a green PR, and a red Compose bump is the one that needs triage into 'Compose changed', 'we were wrong', or 'a new deliberate divergence'. Majors stay manual: a major of any of these is a changed rule set, not a refreshed one.

Minor bumps of the runtime dependency (project.dependencies: pyyaml) automerge. pyproject.toml declares the range `pyyaml>=6.0.2,<7`, so a minor moves only the hash-pinned locks, which is what CI and the container image install, and never what the wheel asks of its users; a major would cross the `<7` ceiling and stays manual. The new lock is exercised on the PR by everything that loads YAML: the test suite, docker-smoke on the built image, and the lockfiles job re-proving the locks reproduce from pyproject.toml. pep621 (the pyproject range) and pip-compile (the lock pin) both tag it project.dependencies, so the grouped python PR is eligible as a whole.

Docker digest refreshes automerge where the three-day gate can actually be enforced, which is Docker Hub only. The images: debian (build stage), postgres (demo compose file), docker/dockerfile (syntax frontend), and busybox and python (the premise validator, via the custom manager above; rule-premises proves every premise on the new digest). Renovate's docker datasource takes releaseTimestamp from Docker Hub's tag_last_pushed and from nowhere else (gcr.io and ghcr.io yield none), and it attaches that timestamp to a digest update only when the tag parses as a version, which is why the build stage is pinned as debian:13-slim rather than trixie-slim (same manifest list). Under the default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour=timestamp-required a digest with no timestamp is pending forever and never even opens a PR, so distroless (gcr.io, tag nonroot), the oss-fuzz builder (gcr.io) and vhs (ghcr.io) are deliberately NOT matched here; the rule after this one labels them `age-gated` and .github/workflows/digest-age-gate.yml merges each once its head commit has been unchanged for 72h (first-seen is never earlier than publish, so that is at least the same wait), and goes away if upstream ever ships a registry-agnostic release timestamp (renovatebot/renovate#39064). The review a human used to do on these PRs is now mechanical: dockerfile-digests fails a per-arch pin, docker-smoke builds and runs the image on amd64 and arm64, and both are required via ci-ok. Verified 2026-10-03 against Renovate 44.132 (lookup/digest.ts, datasource/docker releaseTimestampNote). The branch-stage half of the age check cannot see a digest's timestamp; the last rule in this list covers that.

The digest PRs the age gate owns carry their own label. gcr.io and ghcr.io digests cannot automerge (no release timestamp, see the rule above), but nobody needs to look at them either: .github/workflows/digest-age-gate.yml merges each one once its head commit has been unchanged for 72h. `age-gated` replaces the repo-wide manual-merge for exactly this set, so manual-merge means 'a human has to act' in every case. The gate adds manual-merge to a PR it refuses for a reason other than age (red ci-ok, a conflict, a hand-touched commit, a draft) and removes it again once the PR is clean; a PR whose checks are still running is simply waited for. The gate selects on this label: rename both or neither.

Workaround for renovatebot/renovate#45236 (fix in flight: renovatebot/renovate#46645), scoped to the update types it affects. Renovate checks minimumReleaseAge twice. The lookup stage has the real data: it ages a digest/pinDigest against the newest release matching the current value and, under the default internalChecksFilter=strict, holds the branch back (Dependency Dashboard 'Pending Status Checks') until the age passes; pin and lockFileMaintenance are exempt there by design because they introduce no new release. The branch stage then re-checks from upgrade.releaseTimestamp, which only version updates carry, and under the default timestamp-required marks every one of these update types yellow forever: renovate/stability-days never clears and automerge silently never fires. #933 (lockFileMaintenance, 2026-09-28) sat pending until a human merged it; #786 and #709 had automerged cleanly before the behaviour changed upstream. timestamp-optional here lets the branch stage stand aside for exactly the upgrades it has no data for. It does not shorten any wait: the three-day gate on digests is still enforced at lookup for every image that has a timestamp (Docker Hub), and the images without one are in no automerge rule. Remove once the upstream fix ships. Verified against 44.132 (workers/repository/update/branch/index.ts stability block vs lookup/digest.ts).
